Worktree folders went from 33.3 GB to 6.0 GB, and nothing was lost: every file I removed was already in git, ignored by git, a dev-server log, or first committed on its worktree's own branch.

### Worktrees: 56 seen, 8 left — [report.md](/framework/ai/sessions/2026/10/13/session-730e8a7b/mastermind-repo-slim/worktree-cleanup/report.md)
- ✅ 28 merged worktrees pruned, including `inbox-ranking` as you asked.
- ✅ 14 merged worktrees with leftover changes were salvaged: the changes were committed on their own branch, then the worktree was removed. [manifest.json](/framework/ai/sessions/2026/10/13/session-730e8a7b/mastermind-repo-slim/worktree-cleanup/manifest.json) lists them, and `git worktree add <path> <branch>` brings one back.
- ✅ `wt-task-folders` needed no salvage branch: its HEAD (`a77fb7695`) is already in `michael/dev`.
- ✅ The pool removed `qf-1` to `qf-4` by itself once I unblocked it. It had been stuck for 24 hours on a stale lock file in `qf-1`, and that loop left 150 duplicate `salvage/qf-1-*` branches. I did not delete those, because `pool.md` says salvage branches are never deleted.
- ✅ 24 of 29 half-removed folders deleted, using a new script ([worktree-leftovers.mjs](../../../../../../../../../../Server/worktree-leftovers.mjs)). Five are kept, each with its reason in the report; one holds a local Cloudflare dev database that git never had.
- ⚠️ 8 stay on purpose: 4 pool slots, the locked `qf-5`, and 3 unmerged branches (`orphans`, `readmeaudit`, `refine-demo`). …
